items.title: 67848_Jimmy McPartland oral history interview
items.q: I had gotten the Austin Highschool Gang then. By that time I had Davey Tough... Bud Freeman on tenor saxophone... and we were doing this vaudeville.

ctx.x: He was famous for dancing those steps, yes.

That's it, he showed me a few little things and I started giving a little mugging out there you know. And mugging the face a little bit and oh the number went over great from then on. So that was a nice little tip he gave me.

We did that vaudeville for a little bit. I had gotten the Austin Highschool Gang then. By that time I had Davey Tough, I had Dick Voynow get Davey Tough on drums, my brother on guitar and banjo. My brother-in-law, Jim Lanigan on string bass and Bud Freeman on tenor saxophone and Teschemaker on clarinet and we had Floyd O'Brien on trombone. And we were doing this vaudeville.

items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: it was through Jimmy's effort that ... I got a saxophone because he went to my dad

ctx.x: Well, of course, it was not until I was about 15 that I was to meet at Austin High School, I was to meet the McPartland brothers, Jimmy who is still going very strong, of course, married to Marian Mary McPartland, who is by the way coming over here to England and had a marvelous musical career. I saw Jimmy at Nice last year and he was just as good as ever and in wonderful condition.

Well, anyway, it was through Jimmy's effort that (You know,) I got a saxophone because he went to my dad and he said, I think Bud, he sings and he dances and I think he might have a natural talent for playing and why don't you consider buying him a C-Melody saxophone. That was the instrument one started on, I was not to continue that. We didn't know whether I could really get into playing, so now in the meantime before any of this happened Dave Tough, the great drummer, later to become I thought the best, with…

items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: the McPartland brothers talked to my father -- talked my father into buying me a C-Melody saxophone

ctx.x: We will go now to where I am at Austin High School and I don't have an instrument yet, but the McPartland brothers talked to my father -- talked my father into buying me a C-Melody saxophone, which he bought at -- I think I was 16; yes -- the age of 16 and two years later, I played my first professional job with no study at all on the C-Melody and that was at a place called the Sheboygan Inn in Sheboygan, Wisconsin. It was right on the lake.

Now, there was a pianist by the name of Lyman Woods, who had a trio -- that is, he wanted a trio and he loved Dave Tough -- Dave Tough was his favorite drummer and he wanted an alto saxophone player, or a tenor, anything, a good saxophone player. Dave Tough told him that I was the best C-Melody saxophone player around and actually, I could hardly play. I couldn't play melody. I could play a few notes.
